title: Word Search II
statement_short: Given an m x n board of characters and a list of strings words, return all words on the board. Each word must be constructed from sequentially adjacent cells horizontally or vertically, without reusing any cell.
constraints: m == board.length, n == board[i].length, 1 <= m, n <= 12, 1 <= words.length <= 3 \* 10^4, 1 <= words[i].length <= 10
hint: Grid up to 12x12 and 3 \* 10^4 target words mandate storing words in a Trie to prune DFS backtracking paths early.
why_not: Right: Trie coupled with 2D grid DFS backtracking prunes invalid prefix paths instantly in O(M \* N \* 4^L) worst-case time. Not Backtracking: Pure backtracking without a Trie searches for each of the 30,000 words independently on the grid, causing severe TLE. Not Graph BFS: Level-order grid traversal requires storing full path histories per queue item, taking excessive memory. Not HashMap / Hash Set: Hash sets check complete words, but cannot prune grid search paths at non-matching prefixes.
complexity: O(M \* N \* 4^L) time, O(W \* L) space
